L207: The band ratio method implemented by Legleiter et al. [5]

L220: column with speciﬁc but wavelength dependent attenuation

L223: 
L224: contain water bathymetry information. A more generalized
L225: 
L226: model, which takes advantage of a number of spectral channels
L227: 
L228: could potentially improve bathymetric estimates. However,
L229: 
L230: a speciﬁc model would be difﬁcult to contruct due to the
L231: 
L232: complex and unknown relationship between the spectral bands
L233: 
L234: and the water column response. A non-parametric method

L236:

L239: be preferable, if like the OBRA method the algorithm could

L245: Support vector machine (SVM) is a supervised machine
L246: 
L247: learning algorithm used to analyze patterns within data, and
L248: 
L249: support vector regression (SVR) is a realization of support
L250: vector machine for prediction [11]. SVR is a non-parametric
L251: 
L252: regression method but also a data dependent learning scheme
L253: 
L254: and thus no explicit model is required to fuse the observations
L255:

L259: 
L260: model is generalized, and can be used to estimate any spec-
L261: 
L262: trally related parameters where no explicit physical model
L263: 
L264: exists. A review of support vector machines and regression
L265: can be found in [12]. Bruzzone et al. [13] have estimated
L266: 
L267: biophysical parameters from remotely sensed data using a
L268: 
L269: multiple estimator system which incorporated SVM in com-
L270: 
L271: bination with a multilayer perceptron (MLP) neural network.
L272: 
L273: Camps-Valls et al. [14] utilized the SVR method to estimate
L274: 
L275: ocean chlorophyll concentration with satellite remote sensing
L276: 
L277: data to provide a more accurate, less biased, and noise resistant
L278: 
L279: model.

L281: In this letter, we propose and test using SVR as an al-
L282: ternative method for bathymetric retrieval in order to more
L283: 
L284: accurately account for the nonlinearity existing in the observed
L285: 
L286: hyperspectral data. A conventional band ratio bathymetry
L287: 
L288: retrieval method is used as a baseline for comparison with the
L289: 
L290: proposed SVR method, and a comparison with in-situ water
L291: 
L292: depth observations is presented. To demonstrate the generality
L293: 
L294: of the SVR method, we also evaluate its ability to predict other
L295: 
L296: water column parameters empirically by using it to estimate
L297: water turbidity from hyperspectral imagery. We again compare
L298: 
L299: the results to in-situ measurements of turbidity.

L692: V. D ISCUSSION AND C ONCLUSION
L693: 
L694: In this study, bathymetry extraction using SVR was pro-
L695: posed and applied to two hyperspectral imagery datasets when
L696:

L701: water turbidity.
L702: 
L703: the benthic layer is visible in two distinct ﬂuvial environments.
L704: 
L705: The retrieved water bathymetry was compared to a band ratio
L706: 
L707: method. SVR incorporates all available spectral bands instead
L708: 
L709: of only examining the ratio of a pair of bands. This is impor-
L710: tant, as all spectral bands were inﬂuenced by both benthic re-
L711: 
L712: ﬂection and water attenuation. The band ratio method, OBRA,
L713: 
L714: establishes a physical model and then uses an empirical
L715: 
L716: method to ﬁnd the optimal pair of spectral bands and neglects
L717: 
L718: all other spectral channels. The physics-based water depth
L719: 
L720: retrieval characteristic of OBRA makes it more generalized.
L721: 
L722: The results also show that OBRA provides consistent results
L723: 
L724: with relatively few training samples; however unfortunately its
L725: performance does not improve with an increase in the training
L726: 
L727: sample size. As an empirical method, a band ratio method
L728: 
L729: may not be optimal for the accurate estimation of bathymetry.
L730: 
L731: In contrast SVR does not require a physical model to bridge
L732: 
L733: the observed data with the desired product. The bathymetry
L734: 
L735: retrieved from SVR outperforms OBRA with a lower RMSE
L736: 
L737: and better R 2 for both the Snake and Blue/Colorado Rivers.
L738: 
L739: The increase of training sample size was shown to improve
L740: SVR water depth estimation performance as well. Because
L741: 
L742: no explicit relationship is required between the observations
L743: 
L744: and the estimated physical parameters, SVR can be potentially
L745: 
L746: extended to estimate other spectral based physical parameters.
L747: 
L748: We also demonstrated how SVR can be used to estimate water
L749: 
L750: turbidity, and the results show that hyperspectral imagery can
L751: 
L752: be used to estimate turbidity with a low RMSE and high R 2.
L753: 
L754: For depth determination, the RMSE for both SVR and
L755: OBRA degrade in deeper water (>2.0 m for Snake River,
L756: 
L757: >1.5 m for Blue/Colorado River); this is caused by the
L758: 
L759: nonlinear inﬂuence of the water column radiance in deeper
L760: 
L761: water. However, for both rivers, SVR still outperforms OBRA,
L762: 
L763: likely because of its use of all spectral radiance measurements.
L764: 
L765: Both SVR and OBRA are less effective in the more turbid
L766: 
L767: Blue/Colorado River (SVR has a R 2 of 0.5), however, the
L768: 
L769: estimated water turbidity shows an obvious coherence with the
L770: observed radiance (SVR has a R 2 of 0.87 when estimating
L771: 
L772: turbidity). This is due to the assumption that for spectral
L773: 
L774: bathymetric retrieval the observed benthic radiance is the
L775: 
L776: more dominant term compared to the water column radiance.
L777: 
L778: However, the substantial turbidity of the Blue/Colorado River
L779: 
L780: has resulted in signiﬁcant water column radiance which masks
L781: 
L782: radiance from the benthic layer.
L783: 
L784: In summary, the proposed SVR method is effective at
L785: 
L786: extracting water depths from hyperspectral imagery and out-
L787: performs the band ratio method. Due to its non-parametric
L788: 
L789: formulation, SVR has also been successfully used to retrieve
L790: 
L791: water turbidity from the observed hyperspectral imagery with
L792: 
L793: high coherence with the physical measured water turbidity.
